chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majilawayh narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best of worship is saying: There is no god except Allah.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah (declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is considered the best act of worship in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the declaration of divine unity, 'La ilaha illa Allah,' as the pinnacle of worship, emphasizing its foundational role in Shia theology as both a verbal affirmation and a state of being. This hadith underscores the concept of *Tawhid* not merely as a creed but as the essence of all devotional acts, linking the believer's internal conviction with external practice. The emphasis on this specific phrase highlights its status as the key to Paradise and the criterion for distinguishing true monotheism from mere ritualism.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 10.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his forefathers that the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.s.) said:
(Saying) ‘There is no God except Allah’ is the best worship act.
